The oil supply structure is intended for use in a planetary gear device. In this arrangement, the planetary gear device includes a carrier that supports a plurality of planetary gears. A tubular body is provided so as to rotate together with the carrier, thereby forming part of the rotating structure of the planetary gear device.

The tubular body is formed with a lubricating oil introduction port. This introduction port serves as an inlet through which lubricating oil is supplied to the planetary gear device. By delivering oil through the tubular body, lubrication can be directed efficiently to the components that require it, such as the planetary gears, bearings, shafts, and other sliding or rotating portions.

An annular body is arranged around the tubular body and is configured to slide relative to the tubular body. The annular body includes a lubricating oil supply passage. This supply passage is positioned so that it communicates with the lubricating oil introduction port formed in the tubular body. As a result, lubricating oil supplied through the annular body can be transferred into the tubular body and then introduced into the planetary gear device.

To help maintain proper oil flow and prevent leakage, a pair of seal rings is provided. These seal rings are positioned on both axial sides of the lubricating oil introduction port. By sealing the region around the introduction port, the seal rings define an oil supply area between the tubular body and the annular body and help ensure that lubricating oil is directed into the introduction port rather than escaping along the sliding interface.

In addition, bypass passages and pressure reduction mechanisms are provided between the tubular body and the annular body. These features control the flow of lubricating oil and help regulate pressure in the oil supply region. The bypass passages allow oil to flow in a controlled manner around or past certain sealed regions, while the pressure reduction mechanisms reduce excessive oil pressure that may develop between the tubular body and the annular body. This configuration helps stabilize lubrication performance, reduce load on the seal rings, suppress oil leakage, and improve the reliability and durability of the planetary gear device.

An oil supply structure for a planetary gear device is configured to supply lubricating oil to components of the planetary gear device in a controlled and reliable manner. The structure includes a rotating tubular body that rotates together with a rotating member of the planetary gear device. The rotating tubular body is provided with a lubricating oil introduction port through which lubricating oil is introduced into the interior of the oil supply structure.

An annular body is disposed around the rotating tubular body so as to be slidable relative to the rotating tubular body. The annular body includes a communicating supply passage that communicates with the lubricating oil introduction port of the rotating tubular body. Lubricating oil introduced through the introduction port is guided through the communicating supply passage and is then supplied toward lubrication target portions of the planetary gear device, such as gears, bearings, shafts, pinion supports, or other sliding and rotating portions requiring lubrication.

Seal rings are arranged between the rotating tubular body and the annular body. These seal rings define and seal oil passages so that lubricating oil can be directed to the intended supply passage while leakage to unintended regions is reduced. The seal rings also help maintain oil pressure in the supply passage, thereby improving the efficiency with which lubricating oil is delivered to the planetary gear device.

In addition to the main communicating supply passage, bypass passages are provided around the seal-ring regions. These bypass passages allow a portion of the lubricating oil to flow around or near the seal rings. However, if excessive oil flows through these bypass passages, oil pressure may decrease in the main supply passage, and the sealing performance of the seal rings may deteriorate. Excessive flow near the seal rings may also increase oil agitation, cause unnecessary leakage, or interfere with stable lubrication of the planetary gear device.

To address this issue, pressure reduction mechanisms are provided in association with the bypass passages or with regions near the seal rings. Each pressure reduction mechanism is configured to restrict, reduce, or regulate the flow of lubricating oil passing around the seal-ring regions. For example, the pressure reduction mechanism may include a narrowed passage, an orifice, a stepped passage, a labyrinth-shaped passage, a throttling portion, or another flow-resistance structure. By increasing flow resistance in the bypass passage, the pressure reduction mechanism limits the amount of lubricating oil that bypasses the seal-ring region.

As a result, lubricating oil is more effectively directed through the intended communicating supply passage and toward the lubrication target portions of the planetary gear device. The amount of oil flowing around the seal rings is controlled, and excessive pressure loss in the oil supply system is suppressed. This improves lubrication control, helps maintain sufficient oil pressure, and enhances the sealing performance of the seal rings.

The oil supply structure therefore enables stable lubrication of the planetary gear device while reducing unnecessary leakage and oil loss. By managing the flow of lubricating oil around the seal-ring regions, the structure improves the durability and reliability of the planetary gear device and contributes to efficient operation of the overall power transmission system.

**An Oil Supply**

An oil supply is an important resource for many countries, industries, and households. Oil is used to produce fuel for cars, airplanes, ships, and machinery. It is also used in manufacturing products such as plastics, chemicals, and synthetic materials. Because of this, a steady oil supply helps support transportation, trade, and economic growth.

However, oil supply can be affected by many factors. Political conflicts, natural disasters, changes in production, and global demand can all influence how much oil is available. When the supply of oil decreases, prices often rise, making fuel and goods more expensive. On the other hand, when oil supply is high, prices may fall.

Many countries try to secure reliable oil supplies by producing oil domestically, importing it from other nations, or storing reserves for emergencies. At the same time, there is growing interest in renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and hydropower. These alternatives can help reduce dependence on oil and lower environmental impact.

In conclusion, an oil supply plays a major role in modern life and the global economy. Managing it carefully is essential, while also developing cleaner and more sustainable energy solutions for the future.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical description of an oil lubrication structure for a planetary gear mechanism where oil is supplied through an annular body to an introduction port in a carrier-side tubular body, with seals and flow-limiting pressure reduction mechanisms.
counterfactuals.output:
An oil lubrication structure for a planetary gear mechanism includes an annular oil supply body disposed around a carrier-side tubular body. Lubricating oil is delivered from an external oil passage into the annular body and then introduced into an introduction port formed in the tubular body, which communicates with internal oil passages of the carrier for supplying oil to planetary gear support portions, bearings, and meshing gear regions.

Seal members are arranged on opposite axial sides of the introduction port between the annular body and the tubular body to define a sealed annular oil chamber and suppress leakage of supplied oil. A pressure reduction mechanism is provided in the oil flow path upstream of, within, or downstream of the annular body. The pressure reduction mechanism restricts the flow passage area, such as by an orifice, throttling groove, labyrinth passage, or clearance restriction, thereby reducing oil pressure and limiting the amount of oil supplied to the carrier. Multiple pressure reduction mechanisms may be arranged in parallel or series to balance lubrication performance with suppression of excessive oil flow, drag loss, and seal load.

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide an abstract-like summary of a mechanical invention for supplying lubricating oil to planetary gears, featuring a tubular body rotating with the carrier, an annular body sliding on it, axial seal rings, bypass passages around the seals, and mechanisms that reduce oil pressure or limit oil flow.
counterfactuals.output: A lubricating oil supply device for planetary gears includes a tubular body that rotates integrally with a planetary carrier and an annular body mounted around the tubular body so as to be axially slidable. The annular body cooperates with axial seal rings to define an oil supply path for delivering lubricating oil to the planetary gear region while maintaining sealing contact during relative movement. To prevent excessive pressure buildup caused by axial displacement, centrifugal effects, or variations in supplied oil quantity, bypass passages are provided around the axial seal rings, allowing oil to escape or circulate past the sealed portions when necessary. The device further includes pressure-reducing or flow-limiting mechanisms, such as throttling passages, relief paths, or controlled clearances, that lower the oil pressure acting on the seals or restrict the amount of oil delivered. This arrangement improves lubrication reliability for the planetary gears while reducing seal load, suppressing leakage or wear, and stabilizing oil supply under varying rotational and operating conditions.

counterfactuals.output:
## Formal Patent Language

### Abstract

A lubrication arrangement for a planetary gear carrier includes a rotatable tubular body configured to rotate about an axis and a stationary annular body disposed radially adjacent to the tubular body. Lubricating oil is transferred from the stationary annular body into the rotating tubular body through an annular transfer region that is sealed on both axial sides by respective sealing elements. At least one bypass passage is provided in fluid communication with the annular transfer region, and at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor is arranged adjacent to, or axially outside of, one or both sealing elements. The bypass passage and flow restrictor reduce oil pressure acting on the sealing elements and thereby improve sealing performance and service life while permitting reliable oil supply to the rotating planetary gear carrier.

---

### Independent Claim

1. A lubrication system for a planetary gear carrier, comprising:  
   
   a rotatable tubular body of the planetary gear carrier, the rotatable tubular body being configured to rotate about a rotational axis and having an oil receiving passage;  
   
   a stationary annular body arranged at least partially around the rotatable tubular body and having an oil supply passage configured to receive lubricating oil from a stationary oil source;  
   
   an annular oil transfer region formed between the stationary annular body and the rotatable tubular body, the annular oil transfer region being configured to communicate lubricating oil from the oil supply passage of the stationary annular body to the oil receiving passage of the rotatable tubular body;  
   
   a first seal arranged on a first axial side of the annular oil transfer region and a second seal arranged on a second axial side of the annular oil transfer region, such that the annular oil transfer region is sealed axially between the first seal and the second seal;  
   
   at least one bypass passage arranged to conduct lubricating oil away from a region adjacent to at least one of the first seal and the second seal; and  
   
   at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor arranged in fluid communication with the at least one bypass passage, the at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor being positioned proximate to, or axially outside of, at least one of the first seal and the second seal,  
   
   wherein the at least one bypass passage and the at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor are configured to reduce oil pressure acting on the at least one of the first seal and the second seal.

---

### Dependent Claims

2. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the rotatable tubular body is a shaft-like portion of a planetary gear carrier configured to support at least one planet gear pin.

3. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the oil receiving passage of the rotatable tubular body is fluidly connected to at least one lubrication channel configured to supply oil to a bearing of a planet gear.

4. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the stationary annular body surrounds an outer circumferential surface of the rotatable tubular body.

5. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the annular oil transfer region comprises an annular groove formed in at least one of the stationary annular body and the rotatable tubular body.

6. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the first seal and the second seal are arranged axially on opposite sides of the oil supply passage.

7. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one bypass passage bypasses one of the first seal and the second seal.

8. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one bypass passage comprises a first bypass passage associated with the first seal and a second bypass passage associated with the second seal.

9. The lubrication system of claim 8, wherein each of the first bypass passage and the second bypass passage includes a respective pressure-reducing flow restrictor.

10. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor comprises an orifice.

11. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor comprises a throttling gap.

12. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor comprises a calibrated restriction bore.

13. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor is arranged axially outside the first seal relative to the annular oil transfer region.

14. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor is arranged axially outside the second seal relative to the annular oil transfer region.

15. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one pressure-reducing flow restrictor is arranged between the annular oil transfer region and one of the first seal and the second seal.

16. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one bypass passage is formed in the stationary annular body.

17. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one bypass passage is formed in the rotatable tubular body.

18. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one bypass passage is formed at an interface between the stationary annular body and the rotatable tubular body.

19. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the at least one bypass passage is configured to discharge oil to a low-pressure region of a transmission housing.

20. The lubrication system of claim 1, wherein the pressure-reducing flow restrictor is configured to maintain pressure in the annular oil transfer region sufficient to supply oil to the rotatable tubular body while lowering pressure at the first seal or the second seal.

---

### Additional Independent Apparatus Claim

21. A planetary gear assembly, comprising:  
   
   a planetary gear carrier having a rotatable tubular portion;  
   
   at least one planet gear rotatably supported by the planetary gear carrier;  
   
   a stationary annular oil feed member arranged coaxially with the rotatable tubular portion;  
   
   an oil transfer chamber disposed between the stationary annular oil feed member and the rotatable tubular portion, the oil transfer chamber being sealed by a pair of axially spaced seals;  
   
   an oil feed path extending from the stationary annular oil feed member through the oil transfer chamber into the rotatable tubular portion; and  
   
   a pressure relief arrangement comprising at least one bypass flow path and at least one flow restrictor, the pressure relief arrangement being disposed adjacent to or axially outward of at least one of the pair of axially spaced seals,  
   
   wherein the pressure relief arrangement is configured to limit pressure applied to the at least one of the pair of axially spaced seals during transfer of oil from the stationary annular oil feed member to the rotatable tubular portion.

---

### Method Claim

22. A method of supplying lubricating oil to a planetary gear carrier, comprising:  
   
   delivering lubricating oil from a stationary annular body to an annular transfer region between the stationary annular body and a rotating tubular body of the planetary gear carrier;  
   
   sealing the annular transfer region on opposite axial sides using first and second seals;  
   
   transferring lubricating oil from the annular transfer region into an oil passage of the rotating tubular body;  
   
   conducting a portion of the lubricating oil through at least one bypass passage located adjacent to or axially outside of at least one of the first and second seals; and  
   
   reducing pressure of the portion of the lubricating oil by passing the portion of the lubricating oil through at least one flow restrictor, thereby reducing oil pressure acting on the at least one of the first and second seals.

---

### Description-Style Patent Wording

In one embodiment, lubricating oil is supplied from a stationary annular member to a rotating tubular portion of a planetary gear carrier. The stationary annular member may be fixed relative to a transmission housing, whereas the tubular portion rotates with the planetary gear carrier about a central axis. An annular oil transfer space is formed between the stationary annular member and the tubular portion. The annular oil transfer space is bounded in the axial direction by two sealing members positioned on opposite axial sides of the oil transfer space.

Oil supplied to the stationary annular member enters the annular oil transfer space and is communicated into one or more radial or axial passages formed in the rotating tubular portion. The passages may direct oil to bearings, pins, gears, or other components of the planetary gear set requiring lubrication.

To reduce the pressure load on the sealing members, one or more bypass paths are provided. Each bypass path may be positioned near a sealing member or axially outside a sealing member relative to the oil transfer space. A pressure-reducing flow restrictor is provided in association with the bypass path. The flow restrictor may be formed as an orifice, throttle bore, annular clearance, calibrated passage, labyrinth restriction, or other restricted flow feature. The bypass path and flow restrictor permit controlled leakage or diversion of oil so that the pressure acting directly on the adjacent seal is reduced while adequate oil pressure remains available for delivery into the rotating tubular body.

The arrangement permits reliable transfer of oil from a non-rotating component to a rotating planetary gear carrier while reducing seal wear, seal extrusion, frictional losses, and leakage caused by excessive pressure at the axial seals.
